tellings.difference: This telling adds that the Roswell crash materials were reportedly taken to Wright-Patterson in 1947, and it leaves out the nuclear test facility and the Blue Book role.
tellings.link_reason: The telling and the story are both Jesse Michels's place-lore about Wright-Patterson AFB. Both say the base became an anti-gravity research center in the 1950s, so they make the same core claim about the same site and era.

as_told.title: Wright-Patterson AFB: Roswell materials and anti-gravity research

plain: A podcast host named Jesse Michels describes Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio as a place with a hidden history, saying that in the 1950s it became a nuclear engineering test site and a research centre for antigravity, meaning ways to make craft overcome gravity without ordinary engines. He says it was also home to Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s. In another episode he tells it a little differently: he leaves out the nuclear work and Blue Book, and adds that it is where wreckage from Roswell, a reported 1947 crash in New Mexico, was said to have been taken, which would make the base a likely centre for any secret study of unknown craft.
